standalone_math_proof.argument: Set x=c(t₀). Since hc is a genuine derivative, c is continuous at t₀. For any relative neighborhood W of x in s, ambient continuity puts c(t) into an ambient neighborhood witnessing W, while hcs puts it into s, for t close enough to t₀. Hence c tends to x in 𝓝[s]x. Pull back the relative equality germ of f and g to obtain equality of f∘c and g∘c near t₀.
standalone_math_proof.lean:
have hcts : Tendsto c (𝓝 t₀) (𝓝[s] (c t₀)) :=
  tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff.mpr ⟨hc.continuousAt, hcs⟩
have hcomp : (f ∘ c) =ᶠ[𝓝 t₀] (g ∘ c) := hfg.comp_tendsto hcts

standalone_math_proof.argument: The assumptions hf and hg certify that the chosen fderiv maps are actual continuous linear Fréchet derivatives. Chain each with the actual one-parameter derivative hc. The image curves have genuine velocities Df(x)[v] and Dg(x)[v]. No image-curve derivative equality is assumed.
standalone_math_proof.lean:
have hfc := hf.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t₀ hc
have hgc := hg.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t₀ hc

standalone_math_proof.argument: Local equality transfers the first genuine derivative witness to g∘c. This same image curve also has the second witness; uniqueness yields Df(x)[v]=Dg(x)[v]. Normed spaces need no completeness or finite-dimensional hypothesis for these arguments.

For the source situation use s=M, t₀=0, x=c(0), f=F̄ and g=F̂ after harmless totalization outside their open neighborhoods. Smoothness supplies the actual derivatives, c is smooth/feasible, and both extensions equal F on the common relative neighborhood. The equality then reproduces the explicit extension verification. Identifying every tangent vector and the intrinsic target-tangent differential still requires separate formal adapters.
